facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs told the Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs that it made progress on online birth registration in the fourth quarter of 2025/26; the meeting report names no digital system for registering deaths.

The Department of Home Affairs reported progress on online birth registration under its Administration programme in the fourth quarter of 2025/26 (January to March 2026), in which that programme met 14 of 22 targets; the meeting report gives no figure for the progress.

The Department of Home Affairs reported that its fourth-quarter 2025/26 target for automated birth registration was not achieved, attributing the missed Administration targets to legal, procurement and interdepartmental processes.

The Department of Home Affairs carries online birth registration and automated birth registration as targets of its own Administration programme and reports on them to Parliament in its fourth-quarter 2025/26 performance report.

systems.tiers: 975,754 cards issued in the quarter; applications also processed at bank branches

note: No made or offices fact: the meeting report does not say where the birth entry is made or how many offices or facilities make it. Also stated: 174,649 births registered within 30 calendar days in the quarter; the chairperson of the Refugee Appeals Authority said Civic Services processes remain largely manual and that Home Affairs systems are not integrated enough to identify deaths; an official said future digitisation would link death registration to the asylum system; a Member asked for implementation timelines for online birth registration and no answer is recorded. Both systems are classed from their names, which is all the report gives of them.
